name: niubash-release-preinstall
description: Release CI pre-install manifest (niubash#189, extended by niubash#209, pinned by niubash#312). The release workflow verifies each entry's pinned artifact SHA-256 against the wpm index (wpm info --json), then installs every verified entry of `packages` into the staged WinuxCmd root with `winuxcmd wpm install <name> --root <staged-root> --yes` — wpm itself re-verifies the downloaded zip against its index entry, so pin == index == downloaded bytes — and finally materializes every entry of `shims` as a winuxcmd.exe hardlink in usr\bin. The staged root also carries `winuxcmd-shim.exe` (staged after the installs so package shims keep linking winuxcmd.exe, which needs no shipped .wpm state) so the release zip can replace a stale package-shim forwarder on upgrade (niubash#466/#468). The package index lives in unixwin/wpm-source (index.json); wpm itself ships inside winuxcmd.exe (`winuxcmd wpm ...`), so no separate wpm.exe is needed.

packages.name: gawk
packages.purpose:
GNU Awk 5.4.1. bash-it plugins and completions hard-depend on awk (the gradle completion pipes through `awk '{print $1}'` on every use); gawk IS the GNU implementation, so plugin scripts written against GNU awk keep their dialect. The wpm `gawk` package is layout=shim: the payload (gawk.exe, awk.exe, and the DLLs its import closure requires - libgmp-10, libmpfr-6, libreadline8, and the transitively imported libncurses6 + libgcc_s_dw2-1; revision unixwin2 restores the last two after unixwin1 dropped them on a direct-import reading and gawk died with 0xC0000135 on clean machines - wpm-artifacts#2, release run 39233051251) lands in <root>\opt\gawk and usr in\gawk.exe is a winuxcmd.exe hardlink shim that forwards there. Line endings (niubash#467): the payload itself is a text-mode mingw build whose CRT rewrites 
 as 
 on write and folds 
 into 
 on read, while every winuxcmd applet does binary stdio - so the LF contract lives in the FORWARDER, not the payload: the bundled winuxcmd.exe/winuxcmd-shim.exe splice `-v BINMODE=3` ahead of the forwarded argv for awk/gawk (this build carries gawk's BINMODE feature but ignores the BINMODE environment variable; the -v assignment is the only lever, and a user's own -v BINMODE=... still wins because it lands later). layout=shim is therefore load-bearing, not cosmetic - a flat payload mapping onto usr in would bypass the adapter and ship CRLF. Requires a bundled WinuxCmd carrying the adapted forwarder (WinuxCmd-side fix for unixwin/niubash#467); the staged verify asserts the raw output bytes, so a release whose bundled forwarder lacks the adapter fails its x64 gate.

packages.name: niugit
packages.purpose: Niu-git 2.56.0.1 (native Windows git without MSYS; real git-for-windows C source built with MSVC, no POSIX layer). The full plugin distro (oh-my-bash, omb-theme-robbyrussell, bash-it, bash-completion, bash-preexec) installs every entry through git clone/pull, so a fresh machine without git.exe on PATH failed all five with 'failed to run git; is git.exe on PATH?' (niubash#209). Bundling niugit removes the hard dependency on the user's environment. 2.56.0.1 is layout=flat: the payload lands under <root>\opt\niugit (mingw64/ + etc/) and mingw64/bin/git.exe is mapped straight onto usr\bin\git.exe, so the git on PATH IS the git binary - no launcher, no winuxcmd dispatch hop, and git --version drops from 72-83 ms to ~14 ms (Git Bash: 45-103 ms). Requires WinuxCmd 1.1.9 or newer in the same release (wpm#1183: POSIX-unlink hardlink break, without which the flat mapping cannot replace the usr\bin hardlink). It is schannel-only TLS with no bundled shell/perl (shell-script parts of git run on niubash's sh) and accepts POSIX-shaped (/d/...) path args.

packages.name: ripgrep
packages.purpose: Ripgrep 15.2.0 (`rg`). A common interactive/search tool users expect right after first setup; shipped so the out-of-the-box shell has modern search without a network fetch (niubash#209). Single static rg.exe payload in <root>\opt\ripgrep with command `rg` registered. Unlike niugit/gawk, the wpm index carries a windows-arm64 artifact too, so this one pre-installs on BOTH Windows legs.

packages.name: fd
packages.purpose: fd 10.4.2. The find counterpart to ripgrep; same rationale (niubash#209): bundled at CI time so users never need a network install for the basics. Single static fd.exe payload in <root>\opt\fd with command `fd` registered, with a windows-arm64 artifact in the index as well.

shims.name: awk
shims.reason: bash-it calls plain `awk`, not `gawk`. The wpm gawk package only registers `commands: [gawk]`, so wpm alone leaves usr\bin without an awk.exe and winuxcmd has no awk builtin to catch the name. The release step hardlinks usr\bin\awk.exe to usr\bin\winuxcmd.exe (exactly what wpm's create_package_shims does); the shim dispatcher then forwards `awk` to opt\gawk\awk.exe from the package payload. This mirrors how MSYS presents gawk as awk.

notes: x64 fail-closed, other legs fail-open (owner decision, niubash#468): on the windows-x64 release leg every manifest package MUST pass its pin check and install, and every manifest shim MUST materialize — any failure fails the release job outright. A silently skipped gawk preinstall once shipped a 1.4.1 without opt\gawk or the usr\bin shims and left 1.4.0-era awk.exe/gawk.exe copies behind (niubash#468). Non-primary legs keep the fail-open contract: a failed install is a loud warning (GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY + ::warning), never a release blocker; users can always run `winuxcmd wpm install <name>` against an installed package, and arm64 legs skip gawk/niugit by design (no arm64 artifacts in the index).

Pin contract (niubash#312): every package entry carries `version` plus a `sha256` map keyed by wpm arch (windows-x64 / windows-arm64). The release workflow refuses to install a package whose live-index artifact digest does not equal the pin — that failure takes the same loud fail-open path as a transport failure, so a release's contents cannot silently drift with the index state of the build minute. Pins were recorded from unixwin/wpm-source main @ dbf971d (official-2026.10.13); bump them deliberately, together with `version`.

Commands contract: every package entry carries `commands`, mirroring the wpm index's `commands` field — wpm materializes a usr\bin shim per registered command (niugit ships git.exe, ripgrep ships rg.exe), never per package name, and the release verify step asserts on these (plus the shims entries), not on package names.

Architecture: niugit and gawk exist as windows-x64 artifacts only in the wpm index; on the arm64 release leg those installs fail by design and the leg ships without them. ripgrep and fd carry windows-arm64 artifacts and pre-install on both legs. The post-package verify step hard-asserts only what the pre-install step reported as installed, per the fail-open contract.

No symlinks, ever: shims are winuxcmd.exe hardlinks (copies on file systems without hardlink support). The issue red lines stand - no archive formats are added, no symbolic links are created, and the runtime never downloads binaries (the assembly happens here, in CI).
The staged package ships <root>\usr\bin shims and the <root>\opt payload tree only - never the .wpm state directory (cache/staging/index).

gawk pin history: v1.4.0 shipped 5.4.1 (25373ae8..., full five-DLL payload); the 1.4.1 prep moved to 5.4.1-unixwin1 (afdce80f..., slimmed) and run 39233051251 failed its staged verify with STATUS_DLL_NOT_FOUND — the slimming had dropped transitively-imported DLLs (wpm-artifacts#2). This pin is 5.4.1-unixwin2, published with the known-good payload bytes (sha256 equal to the v1.4.0-era full artifact; wpm-source#97 carries the index entry). DEPENDENCY: the wpm-source entry (#97) and the wpm-artifacts release must land before a re-tagged release ships gawk again; until then the pin check fail-opens (loud warning, the release ships without gawk per the fail-open contract) — it can never silently install bytes this manifest did not pin (niubash#312).

awk/gawk line-ending floor (niubash#467): the pinned payload keeps its shipped bytes — the CRLF fix lives in the bundled winuxcmd.exe/winuxcmd-shim.exe forwarder (adapted-command argv splice: -v BINMODE=3). Bundling a WinuxCmd older than the release carrying that adapter re-ships text-mode gawk, so the winuxcmd-pin.json bump and this manifest are one change window; the staged verify's raw-byte probes are the fail-closed guard for that ordering (a PowerShell native capture strips \r — string equality alone can never see the regression, which is how the text-mode build shipped).

excluded.name: goawk
excluded.reason: Owner decision (gawk only): goawk is forbidden in the pre-install manifest. Plugins target GNU awk; a second awk dialect on PATH is a compatibility hazard, not an enhancement. (The separate wpm `awk` package is likewise not installed: it is the same upstream artifact as `gawk` — gawk-5.4.1, same SHA-256 — and the awk command is provided by the shims entry above.)

excluded.name: bzip2
excluded.reason: Owner decision: no compression tools in the pre-install manifest. Users install bzip2 themselves via `winuxcmd wpm install bzip2` when they need it.

excluded.name: gzip
excluded.reason: Owner decision: no compression tools in the pre-install manifest. Users install gzip themselves via `winuxcmd wpm install gzip` when they need it.

excluded.name: link
excluded.reason: Owner directive: FORBIDDEN FOREVER. The name collides with the MSVC link.exe toolchain binary; it must never appear in packages or shims of any manifest revision.
